svg.desc: Banner for a paper on the largest eigenvalue of the normalised distance Laplacian. Left: a schematic of the best networks, two nearly complete clusters of n/2 nodes each joined by a path of about √(3n) links, with the extremal eigenvector drawn above it: +1 on one cluster, −1 on the other and falling linearly along the path. Right: the trade-off behind the constant. With a path of s√n links the scaled gap below 2 is 2/s from pairs inside the two ends (dashed, falling) plus 2s/3 from pairs between the path and the ends (dashed, rising); their sum is smallest at s = √3, where it equals 4/√3 ≈ 2.31, below the earlier construction’s 2√2 ≈ 2.83, drawn as a dotted line. Footer: first order as n grows.
svg.text: How close to 2? A balance between two costs
best networks: two dense ends joined by one path; the gap below 2 is 4/√(3n) to first order
Largest eigenvalue of the normalised distance Laplacian · first order as n grows
